item.title: An Algebraic Formulation of Thermality in Nested Rindler Wedges
item.description: arXiv:2610.27007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Padmanabhan and Kolekar had demonstrated the phenomenon of recursive thermality in two dimensional free field theories where the Rindler vacuum appears thermal to an observer accelerated with respect to the Rindler observer. We study the same construction at an algebraic level for conformal field theories. At each step, a parent wedge is conformally mapped to a reference Minkowski spacetime, where a new right Rindler wedge and its left sibling are selected. We illustrate that under the Bisognano--Wichmann property, thermality holds at every generation: the state associated with a parent wedge becomes a KMS state when restricted to its right child. Further, using the modular structure of the wedge and its causal sibling, we identify the sibling algebra with the modular commutant and derive the corresponding recursive modular flow explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Waheed A. Dar, Prince A. Ganai, Nirmalya Kajuri

item.title: Nambu-Goldstone Bosons and Quantum Fisher Information
item.description: arXiv:2610.27054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum Fisher matrix and geometric tensor are powerful tools for quantifying the nature of quantum systems. Unfortunately, the formalism needed to compute these quantities is opaque and has limited the development of physical intuition for their behavior, even in the ground state. For quantum systems with continuous symmetries, we know the ground state can be understood in a model-independent and intuitive way from the correlation functions of conserved currents and charges. In this paper, we demonstrate an equivalence between the quantum Fisher matrix associated with the ground states of systems with continuous symmetries and the Nambu-Goldstone. bosons produced by broken generators. We will show that the information metric defined by the Fisher matrix is the same as the Zamolodchikov metric that defines the coset space of the system. Next we show that the Uhlmann curvature associated with multi-parameter estimation is the same as the charge density matrix that defines the difference between type-A and type-B Nambu-Goldstone bosons. We demonstrate these connections in several examples and discuss the generalization to finite temperature.
item.dc:creator: Eugene Chen, Daniel Green

item.title: Scale-separated AdS vacua on Riemann-Flat Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supergravity compactifications supported by fluxes and Casimir energy offer a simple strategy to concoct explicit, controlled and isolated vacua with parametric scale separation and soft supersymmetry breaking. Exploiting the special properties of both the Casimir and flux potentials with respect to Laplacian operators in moduli space, we prove that the simplest such class of solutions, given by toroidal compactifications of eleven-dimensional supergravity threaded by any fluxes, always exhibit perturbative instabilities in the form of tachyonic modes below the BF bound. This no-go theorem applies to any toroidal supergravity compactification supported by $p$-form fluxes. We also study compactifications on more general Riemann-flat manifolds (RFM's). Concretely, we find a tachyon-free AdS$_4$ vacuum by compactifying M-Theory on a $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$. This constitutes the first ever example of a fully top-down, perturbatively stable, scale-separated AdS without localized sources.
item.dc:creator: Miquel Aparici, Ivano Basile, Bruno Valeixo Bento, Miguel Montero

item.title: Bilocal flows and universality with field-dependent regulators
item.description: arXiv:2610.27063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many functional renormalization group flows employ a regulator that depends on the fields, as in proper-time and spectrally adjusted flows and in background-independent formulations of gauge theories and quantum gravity. Such a regulator generates additional terms in the flow, and their omission may spoil universality. We introduce bilocal flows, in which the effective action depends on the field and on the cutoff kernel as independent variables. The construction identifies the additional terms, and an exact sum rule shows that the first nontrivial coefficient of the anomalous dimension coincides with that of a fixed-regulator flow for every admissible regulator profile, so that universality is restored. For massless $\lambda\phi^4$ theory with a proper-time regulator, the reduced flow gives a profile-dependent anomalous dimension, while the completed flow gives the universal two-loop coefficient $C_\eta=1/6$ for every profile.
item.dc:creator: Alfio M. Bonanno, Renata Ferrero

item.title: Deconfinement on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ and Axion Domain Walls
item.description: arXiv:2610.27072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nontrivial dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls and compute their tension in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) compactified on a circle with $N$ colors and $F < N$ massless fundamental flavors. In the process, we obtain insights on the $\eta'$ meson's potential in a regime where it is heavy and comparable in mass to other QCD resonances, as in Nature. We employ a center-stabilized compactification of QCD on a small circle of size $L$ with color-flavor twisted boundary conditions for the quarks. We demonstrate that probe particles in color representations of $N$-ality $N/\mathrm{gcd}(N,F)$ are deconfined on the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls whenever $N$ and $F$ are not coprime. This is reminiscent of deconfinement on axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills. Finally, in the double scaling limit $N\rightarrow \infty$ keeping $NL$ and $F$ fixed, the infrared spectrum spans an emergent dimension. We establish that the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls are dual to electrostatic charge distributions in this emergent dimension. This duality allows us to compute their tension analytically and find a different tension scaling at large-$N$ between $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls in QCD and axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills, in center-stabilized compactifications.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Bilisco, Raffaele Tito D'Agnolo, Arthur Platschorre, Pablo Sesma

item.title: Gravitational Path Integral and String Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.27073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational path integral has had many applications in recent years. Using the example of supersymmetric index, which provides one of the most controlled tests of gravitational path integral, we argue that even in this controlled case, naive gravitational path integral cannot produce consistent results beyond low orders. However one can go further using stringy inputs, e.g. the choice of UV cut-off and the choice of correct path integration variable, without having to do full fledged string calculation. We also discuss to what extent we are led to string scale UV cut-off even if we begin with a supergravity theory without an a priori bias towards string theory. This is a review of mostly published results, but we clarify several details.
item.dc:creator: Ashoke Sen

item.title: Classical solitons in anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.27074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study classical soliton solutions in split-signature anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory. Using Zakharov's dressing method, we construct rational lump solitons, which are localised near two-dimensional surfaces, and wall solitons, which have codimension one. We further describe multi-phase solutions which have multiple walls meeting at trivalent junctions and form four-dimensional foam-like structures. Two-pole solutions describe soliton interactions and we find non-trivial colour-dressed phase shifts for wall interactions. We consider the four-dimensional analogue of Ward's lump scattering for the restricted kinematics of coincident poles and show that there are non-trivial interactions in the collinear limit. Finally, we show that the determinant of the soliton matrix provides a $\tau$-function which acts as a potential for gauge-invariant scalar quantities such as the Yang-Mills Lagrangian density.
item.dc:creator: Tristan McLoughlin

item.title: Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.
item.dc:creator: Paul Balavoine, Severin L\"ust

item.title: IR extremality and UV softness in string bootstrap
item.description: arXiv:2610.27084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether string amplitudes can be characterized by extremality within the space of consistent S-matrices is an intriguing question. We address this question within the framework of positivity bootstrap. We compute positivity bounds by minimizing the $F^4$ Wilson coefficient while fixing subleading coefficients, and show that the Veneziano amplitude lies close to the boundary of the allowed region. However, this numerical proximity does not imply exact extremality, as demonstrated by explicit counterexamples. When additional KLT-motivated UV softness is imposed, the Veneziano amplitude is found to uniquely minimize the $F^4$ coefficient for $4\leq D\leq10$, connecting the extremality of the Veneziano amplitude to its stringy UV behavior and offering a new perspective on what makes string theory special.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Lin Wan, Ji-Yang Wang, Shuang-Yong Zhou

item.title: AdS$_2$ from Type IIA on weak G$_2$ manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present and study supersymmetric warped ${\rm AdS}_2 \times {\rm M}_7 \times I$ solutions of Type IIA supergravity, where M$_7$ is a weak G$_2$ holonomy manifold. Locally, the solutions are characterized by a cubic polynomial. We distinguish two branches, Branch 1 and Branch 2, and analyze their global properties, taking flux quantization into account. At the endpoints of the interval $I$ they exhibit either OF1-plane or O8/D8 type of singularities with Branch 1 allowing also for a Spin(7) cone. In the case of zero Romans mass, Branch 1 uplifts to eleven dimensions to ${\rm AdS}_4 \times {\rm M}_7$ whereas Branch 2 uplifts to warped ${\rm AdS}_3 \times {\rm M}_7 \times I$ with OM2-plane type of singularities.
item.dc:creator: Niall T. Macpherson, Achilleas Passias

item.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.27097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of integer partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. The free energy of the interpolating solutions cannot be matched with the on-shell action of any known bulk solution. The $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies can be computed analytically. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Peng, Xuao Zhang, Ziruo Zhang

item.title: A group theoretic calculation of multi-invariants of some stabilizer states
item.description: arXiv:2610.27098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multi-invariants---a multi-partite generalization of Renyi entropies---of simple stabilizer states, for an arbitrary replica symmetry group. We develop a group theoretic technique for evaluating such invariants, which operates on the replica group and involves counting intersections among its cosets. Our techniques streamline the calculations of multi-invariants for graph states with two GHZ-like nodes and for certain generalizations thereof. The methodology developed here is most suitable when the quantum state is simple but flexibility over the replica group is desired.
item.dc:creator: Bartlomiej Czech, Yichen Feng, Jonathan Harper, Xin-Xiang Ju

item.title: Realization of de Sitter spacetime in AdS/CFT
item.description: arXiv:2610.27246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct horizonless, everywhere-regular solitons containing a de~Sitter core inside an asymptotically anti--de~Sitter spacetime, using an ordinary action of Einstein gravity, a Maxwell field, and a charged scalar. The object is a gravitating gauged $Q$-ball whose false-vacuum interior acts as a positive effective cosmological constant, sourcing an inner de~Sitter region joined through a thin wall to a charged, asymptotically AdS exterior. Two general requirements are emphasized: the scalar must lie in a near-false-vacuum (slow-roll--like) regime, and the exterior is driven to the extremal Reissner--Nordstr\"om--AdS locus in the thin-wall limit, in which the wall approaches the common would-be horizon. Since the solution is static and spherically symmetric, it may correspond to a semiclassical charge-$Q$ state of the dual CFT, realizing de~Sitter space approximately within a holographic theory. We also discuss free fluctuations whose de~Sitter--core modes appear as parametrically low-lying excitations above the state, bulk reconstruction, and the near-extremal regime, where finite-${\mathcal N}$ effects are expected to cut off the formal classical throat and replace its independent free-field modes by an interacting near-throat sector.
item.dc:creator: Yasutaka Koga, Keiju Murata, Seiji Terashima

item.title: Classical and Stochastic Trans-Planckian Censorship
item.description: arXiv:2610.27319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The trans-Planckian censorship conjecture (TCC) limits inflation to a deadline of $N_{\rm TCC}=\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H_{\rm end})$ e-folds. We formulate it in stochastic inflation as a bound at confidence $1-\delta$ on the probability that a history outlasts the deadline, with three readings: one worldline, the region grown from one Hubble patch, and the reheated volume. Each reading becomes a closed-form condition, rigorous for a linear roll in leading-order stochastic inflation (for the region, in a branching model) and sharp at leading order in $N_{\rm TCC}$: a linear roll whose classical history lasts $N_{\rm cl}$ e-folds respects the TCC if $1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC}\geq\{2\mathcal{P}_\zeta[w+\ln(1/\delta)/N_{\rm TCC}]\}^{1/2}$, with $w=0$ for a worldline and $w=3$ for a region. On a linear slope without vacuum decay, the worldline and region readings are never weaker than the classical TCC, and on the CMB-normalized attractor all readings agree closely with it, so the bounds on the scale of inflation stand. A classical phase that ends in a flat quantum well, which the overdamped classical TCC excludes, is allowed with a margin of a few e-folds per worldline. Near the onset of eternal inflation, the readings differ. On a linear slope, a region must leave the fraction $\sqrt{6\mathcal{P}_\zeta}$ of the deadline unused at leading order: eternal inflation is excluded for every classical history that uses a finite fraction of the deadline, as is a band of non-eternal slopes, and the slope bound becomes $|V'|>V^{3/2}/[\sqrt2\,\pi(1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC})]$. Per worldline, every slope is allowed, given a margin of a few standard deviations. A false vacuum must decay at about the eternal threshold $\Gamma=9H^4/(4\pi)$ or faster for a region or the volume, but only faster than $3H^4\ln(1/\delta)/(4\pi N_{\rm TCC})$ per worldline. Whether the TCC forbids eternal inflation depends on the reading.
item.dc:creator: Omer Guleryuz

item.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Yamazaki-Hori solution to the Ernst equation can be represented in the Pfaffian form. We also discuss the consequences of this result for Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model.
item.dc:creator: Arsen Melikyan, Aleksandr Pinzul

item.title: Holographic Reconstruction from Broken Conformal Gauge Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.27511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate bulk--boundary structures in $\AdS_4/\CFT_3$ from the viewpoint of gravity as a broken phase of conformal gauge symmetry. A crucial distinction is made between the Euler and Pontryagin characteristic classes. The gauge-theoretic gravitational action contains an Euler sector, whose total-derivative representation gives a boundary form depending on both intrinsic and extrinsic geometry. This structure is different from the Pontryagin descent to the three-dimensional gravitational Chern--Simons functional, whose metric variation gives the Cotton tensor and underlies the mixed boundary conditions studied by de Haro. We perform a Fefferman--Graham expansion of the Euler boundary form in asymptotically $\AdS_4$ spacetime. The normalizable coefficient $g_{(3)ij}$ does not contribute linearly to the finite Euler boundary term: its contribution from the cubic extrinsic- curvature sector vanishes by $\mathrm{Tr}\,g_{(3)}=0$, while curvature-- extrinsic-curvature terms containing $g_{(3)}$ vanish at the conformal boundary. A direct Codazzi analysis additionally shows that the Cotton tensor appears in the asymptotic mixed curvature but its contribution through the tangential-connection boundary variation vanishes for standard Dirichlet data. This indicates two distinct types of bulk--boundary structure: a global/topological Euler relation and a local Pontryagin--Cotton relation. We distinguish this kinematic Cotton appearance from a finite Cotton boundary response and discuss the implications for holographic reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Takeshi Fukuyama

item.title: Learning the open string spectrum with neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.27667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The tree-level open superstring has an integer mass-squared spectrum on linear Regge trajectories. To what extent is this fixed by consistency conditions: locality, analyticity, crossing, unitarity together with the requirement that $2\to2$ scattering minimize the entanglement it generates? Using the local two-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity ($\lambda$-CSDR) we set up a bootstrap treating both the mass-squared spectrum and the partial-wave coefficients as unknowns which lets the machine learning algorithm to learn the mass-squared spectrum and partial-wave coefficients simultaneously, going beyond earlier work in which the spectrum was fixed. Using the local three-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity we obtain, within the class of amplitudes with soft Regge behavior and infinite higher-spin tower, a bound on the leading Wilson coefficients that we compare with existing bounds and trace to spin-0 dominance. We locate the Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude in the allowed region of the Wilson coefficients space. For amplitudes with two-channel crossing symmetry we find that a Non-dual amplitude exhibits a Polchinski-Strassler type transition from Regge to power-law behavior.
item.dc:creator: Debapriyo Chowdhury

item.title: Thermodynamic Supercritical Scaling Law for the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS Black Hole
item.description: arXiv:2610.27824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The phase structure of the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS black holes varies with the spacetime dimension. Within an appropriate parameter range, only the six-dimensional case admits two physical critical points and it is an ideal model for investigating supercritical thermodynamics in black hole systems with multiple critical points. In this study, we investigate the supercritical thermodynamic properties of this model in the extended phase space and construct the supercritical phase diagrams associated with the two critical points. The thermodynamic supercritical scaling analysis for the supercritical crossover lines in the vicinity of both critical points is completed, demonstrating universality. The corresponding coefficients for the external field scaling and the order parameter scaling are obtained, and their physical significance is discussed.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Yi Xia, Zhen-Ming Xu

item.title: Free-field realizations of $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras associated with Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.27853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the recursive construction of free-field realizations proposed by Ide, Ito, and Miyazaki to the $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras $\mathcal{SW} B (n - 1 , n)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (n , n)$, associated with the Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$, respectively. We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.
item.dc:creator: Naozumi Tanabe

item.title: Monodromy line defects on the fuzzy sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.27926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monodromy line defects are of interest in the defect bootstrap program and are dual to electrically charged objects in dual gauge field descriptions. We investigate the Ising monodromy dCFT using a fuzzy sphere regularization, by imposing the twisted boundary condition in the UV. We obtain defect scaling dimensions $\hat \Delta$ and ratios of defect operator expansion (DOE) coefficients using this method. We extend this machinery to the continuous family of $O(2)$ monodromy defects with twist angle $2\pi\nu$. In both cases, the lowest neutral defect scalar lies above dimension one, providing evidence that the monodromy defect reaches a stable dCFT without additional fine tuning.
item.dc:creator: Jiangyuan Qian

item.title: Non-minimal unimodular inflation revisited: Swampland diagnostics and CMB constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.27991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-minimal unimodular inflation in the Einstein frame; the effective potential takes the form $U(\varphi)=U_0(1+\xi\varphi^2/\mpl^2)^{-2}$. We consider the canonical field map and the inflationary observables directly from the Einstein-frame action. The exact potential slow-roll parameters, the leading scalar running, the scalar-amplitude normalization, the e-fold relation, and the end-of-inflation condition are obtained analytically. The model has a nontrivial structural tension: an $\epsilon_V=1$ exit requires $\xi>1/2$, whereas the near-origin slow-roll regime requires $\xi\ll1$ and gives $n_s\simeq1-8\xi$. We next test three distinct swampland diagnostics. The further-refined de Sitter conjecture (FRDSSC) introduces the independent conjectural parameters $a$, $b$, and $q$, while the scalar weak gravity conjecture (SWGC) and its strong form (SSWGC) contain no analogous tunable conjecture parameter in the single-field realization adopted here. All three criteria are evaluated using the canonically normalized Einstein-frame scalar. Analytic limits show that the SWGC is violated at the stationary point for every nonzero $\xi$, whereas the SSWGC at that point requires $\xi\gtrsim0.0643$. In the large-field limit both scalar weak-gravity diagnostics reduce to the same threshold $\xi\ge0.1$. Numerical scans then show that the observationally relevant ACT/P-ACT region does not satisfy either scalar weak-gravity criterion, while the FRDSSC can be satisfied for $a$ close to unity. Consequently, the minimal model can reproduce acceptable $(n_s,r)$ at isolated field values, but this does not constitute a complete 50-60 e-fold inflationary history or simultaneous satisfaction of all three conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Noori Gashti, Mohammad Reza Alipour, Mohammad Ali S. Afshar, Behnam Pourhassan, \.{I}zzet Sakall{\i}, Phongpichit Channuie

item.title: Reconstructing the Goldberg-Palatini Action from Noether Identities
item.description: arXiv:2610.28065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the reconstruction of the first-order gravitational action from the Noether identities associated with diffeomorphism invariance. The independent fields are a symmetric perturbation $\phi^{\mu\nu}$ of the contravariant metric density and a trace-adjusted connection $G^{\lambda}{}_{\mu\nu}$, whose transformation laws are prescribed. For a local action polynomial in these fields, with the gravitational coupling as its only dimensionful constant and each additional field carrying one power of it, a dilatation, which is a particular diffeomorphism, shows that in any dimension $d>2$ the action terminates at most at cubic order, its only possible cubic term being a derivative-free $\phi GG$ vertex. Expanding the kernels of the resulting Lorentz-covariant ansatz in tensor bases gives 31 coefficients for $d\geq 4$. The Noether identities with general diffeomorphisms, expanded order by order in the fields, yield a linear system that eliminates the $\phi\phi$ kernel and determines the remaining coefficients up to an overall normalization, recovering the Goldberg-Palatini action. Since the connection can be eliminated exactly, this also fixes the complete second-order action, with its infinite set of graviton vertices. The construction requires no choice of energy-momentum tensor, the source of ambiguity in the self-coupling approach. The kernel bases, the identities and the solution are given in appendices, and the symbolic computations are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: F. T. Brandt, Augusto C. B. Carvalho

item.title: Possible Microscopic source of torsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.28125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Axial fermionic interactions connect vacuum condensation with torsionful back- grounds. We consider a quartic spin spin interaction whose mean field reduction yields a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian. Its diagonalisation defines a particle and antiparticle condensate, while self consistency determines whether the vacuum devel- ops a non zero axial current. Cutoff, fluctuation and energy conditions delimit the validity of the approximation. When torsion couples to spin, this axial expectation value can provide a microscopic source for an axial torsion background. We then consider mixed Dirac fields on such a background. In the explicit neutrino analysis, metric curvature is neglected while torsion modifies the flavour Bogoliubov coeffi- cients, producing spin dependent oscillation frequencies, condensate densities and CP asymmetries.
item.dc:creator: A. Capolupo, S. Monda, G. Pisacane, A. Quaranta, R. Serao

item.title: Surface defects on lens space and transfer matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.28165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study surface defects in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}_k$ placed on $L(r,1)\times S^1$. The lens space index depends on the fugacities $p$ and $q$, and the effect of the defects on it is captured by difference operators acting on the fugacities and holonomies of flavor symmetries. For theories of type $A_1$ we determine in closed form the difference operators for the basic defects, labeled by $p^r$, $q^r$ and $pq$, and show that for odd $r$ there exist additional elementary defects, whose operators shift the holonomy by one half modulo $r$. All the operators commute, and the elementary operators generate the others. For even $r$ the same holds once the holonomy is extended to a twisted sector. We show that the elementary operators are traces of $L$-operators whose entries generate a Sklyanin algebra, with nome $q^r$ and shift $pq$. The lens space enters only through the parameters of the algebra and through its representation, which is realized on a doubled holonomy label. The $p$- and $q$-type algebras form a lens space version of the elliptic modular double. For class $\mathcal{S}_k$ theories we propose, and test in several ways, that the defect operators are transfer matrices of inhomogeneous spin chains built from these $L$-operators. Throughout, we use the TQFT structure of the lens space index, which follows from S-duality, both to fix and to check the operators.
item.dc:creator: Kazunobu Maruyoshi, Toshihiro Ota, Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: Finite Spectral Recurrences for Loop Integrals in de Sitter and Anti-de Sitter Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.28183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a method that does for loop integrals in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter space what integration-by-parts identities do in flat space. A local, coordinate-free propagator algebra common to both geometries yields exact finite-difference equations in spectral labels; with external points they become differential-difference equations, and at the AdS boundary recover known Witten-diagram relations. Acting line by line, they apply in principle to any diagram. We solve them for the two-loop watermelon, isolating its ultraviolet poles, and for one-loop two- and four-point functions.
item.dc:creator: Bruce A. Bassett, Sergio Cacciatori, Ugo Moschella

item.title: Causality violation in the holographic approach to N=4 SYM theory at finite 't Hooft coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.28319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, correlation functions of the energy-momentum tensor in N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory at large but finite 't Hooft coupling can be studied using higher-derivative corrections to supergravity. We show that the commonly used holographic prescription for correlation functions which is obtained by truncating the equations of motion at order $(\alpha')^3$ implies that the thermal equilibrium state of N=4 SYM theory in the planar limit is dynamically unstable at arbitrarily large finite 't Hooft coupling. The instability is a reflection of the unphysical causality violation brought about by treating perturbatively-derived equations as if they were non-perturbative, analogous to the instability of AdS black branes in five-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet gravity. While other holographic prescriptions for treating the $O(\alpha'^3)$ corrections to supergravity may alleviate the pathology introduced by the truncation, the validity regime of the results obtained by any prescription at $O(\alpha'^3)$ must be limited to the strict perturbative treatment of the $O(\alpha'^3)$ effects on N=4 SYM observables.
item.dc:creator: Alex Buchel, Pavel Kovtun

item.title: Cosmological correlators from the Euclidean sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.28516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new framework for computing late-time cosmological correlators in de Sitter spacetime by analytic continuation from the Euclidean sphere. In this framework, correlators of arbitrary massive scalar fields take the universal form of generalized Euler integrals. Using this representation, we reproduce the results obtained using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism for a range of tree-level and loop diagrams, providing nontrivial checks of the equivalence between the Euclidean and the in-in formalisms. We further show that a Landau analysis of the generalized Euler integrals determines the singularities of the corresponding correlators in momentum space. This framework provides a systematic approach to studying the analytic structure of cosmological correlators.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Katsevich, Zimo Sun

item.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $\delta^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{\delta+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,\Delta}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $\Delta(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $\delta+1={\rm deg}\,\Delta$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.
item.dc:creator: Ya. Kononov, A. Morozov

item.title: Universal Structure of Horizon Formation in Generic Binary Black Hole Mergers
item.description: arXiv:2609.11819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive the local structure of the first common apparent horizon in a generic binary-black-hole merger. This event occurs in the fully nonlinear regime, outside the standard regimes of post-Newtonian inspiral theory and perturbations of a stationary black hole, yet it admits a universal description. Without assuming symmetry, we show that the stability operator of the marginally outer trapped surface must lose invertibility at formation. Outermost stability then implies that the vanishing eigenvalue is the principal one, with a strictly positive eigenfunction. Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction yields square-root branch separation with a shared linear drift. Together these terms give a tilted parabola through linear order in time. The common horizon lies on a smooth marginally outer trapped tube tangent to the formation slice, and nearby later slices intersect it in outer and inner branches whose separation scales as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$. Horizon quantities with a nonzero first response along the zero mode inherit the square-root separation and a shared linear term. We test these predictions in three binary black hole simulations, including an eccentric, precessing, unequal-mass system. In all three, the worldtube geometry and quasilocal scalars follow the predicted scaling. With the next-order term included, free-exponent fits to the surface geometry and quasilocal functionals recover $1/2$ to within half a percent, and diagnostics agree on the formation time within $5\times10^{-5}M$. The correlation between horizon shear and gravitational-wave news suggests that common horizon formation could have a signature in a short segment of the merger waveform.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Cun Xie, Vaishak Prasad

item.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.26892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the QFT-natural prescription in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem $\,$---$\,$ which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system $\,$---$\,$ is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Saurya Das, Samuel L. Braunstein

item.title: Aspects of Anomalies: Fermion Family Constraints, Gravitational Form Factors and Scattering Amplitudes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum anomalies play two complementary roles in quantum field theory: as consistency conditions that constrain the field content of a theory, and as dynamical effects encoded in the analytic structure of correlation functions. This thesis explores both. In the first part, we study the 331 model, in which gauge anomalies cancel across families rather than within each one. Combined with QCD asymptotic freedom, this fixes the number of fermion generations to three. We analyze the model's symmetry breaking, scalar and flavor sectors, and its TeV-scale Landau pole. We then study the collider phenomenology of its exotic quarks, showing that the pair production of heavy quarks decaying into doubly-charged vector bileptons gives a clean same-sign dimuon plus b-jets signature, observable at a 100 TeV collider but not at the LHC. Finally, we introduce the left-right symmetric 33311 extension, which preserves the family-number constraint and avoids proton decay. In the second part, we use conformal field theory in momentum space to study the chiral, gravitational and conformal anomalies. We construct a complete off-shell parametrization of the non-Abelian TJJ correlator in perturbative QCD, identifying the dilaton-like anomaly pole. For the AVV, ATT and TJJ vertices, we prove mass-independent anomaly sum rules for the spectral density, showing that the anomaly pole is not an asymptotic particle state. We apply the TJJ insertion to the pion gravitational form factors at large momentum transfer with Sudakov resummation: the anomaly feeds mainly into the D-term and the trace form factor, improving agreement with lattice QCD. Lastly, sewing two anomaly vertices through graviton exchange, we show that the trace anomaly activates a gauge-invariant scalar gravitational channel, giving a double-copy-like structure in photon and graviton scattering.
item.dc:creator: Dario Melle

item.title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
item.description: arXiv:2610.26908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.
item.dc:creator: Yuuki Sugiyama, Kazushige Ueda

item.title: Linear Structure, Convergence and Resurgence of Hydrodynamic Transseries
item.description: arXiv:2610.26958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an exact formulation for the solution of Bjorken expanding relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a constant relaxation time and derive its late time transseries structure. The two fundamental modes of the linear auxiliary equation separate the hydrodynamic contribution from the exponentially suppressed transient mode. We show that this single transient mode generates the entire hierarchy of nonperturbative sectors through nonlinear mode mixing, while its decay explains the loss of initial condition dependence and the emergence of late time hydrodynamic attractor behavior. The hydrodynamic gradient expansion is factorially divergent for generic values of the transport parameter but converges at the discrete values $a=N^2$, where the auxiliary asymptotic expansions terminate. We further determine the exact Stokes constant of the auxiliary linear equation and establish its relation to the logarithmic Borel singularity coefficient. The vanishing of the Stokes constant at these exceptional values establishes a direct connection between auxiliary series termination, hydrodynamic convergence, and Stokes decoupling between the hydrodynamic and the nonhydrodynamic transient sector.
item.dc:creator: Qi Zhou, Enke Wang, Hui Zhang

item.title: Gravitational baryogenesis in asymptotically safe gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.27020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gravitational baryogenesis in asymptotically safe gravity is considered. Two baryogenesis interactions are explored and their effects on the baryon-to-entropy ratio are discussed during the radiation era. The model's parameters are constrained with the current observational data, indicating these constructions may provide viable explanations for the observed baryon asymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Rong-Jia Yang

item.title: Nonlinear Response of Schwarzschild Black Holes at Arbitrary Perturbative Order
item.description: arXiv:2610.27048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish recursive integration-by-parts identities that symbolically reduce the inhomogeneous solutions of the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equation to a small set of master integrals, yielding the nonlinear response kernels of Schwarzschild black holes at arbitrary perturbative order. We further derive a closed ODE system that enables rapid, accurate, and stable numerical evaluation of these master integrals. To demonstrate our result, we compute quadratic, cubic, and quartic quasinormal-mode coupling coefficients as special cases of the response kernels.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Chen, Yu-Cun Xie

item.title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.27059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Hengameh Bagherian, Matthew Reece, Lian-Tao Wang, Huangyu Xiao

item.title: Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.27062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.
item.dc:creator: Till Bargheer, Tengis Batmunkh, Paul Ryan

item.title: R\'enyi multi-entropy of graph states and the $n -> 1$ limit
item.description: arXiv:2610.27080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: R\'enyi multi-entropy extends the R\'enyi entropy to pure states of more than two parties. It is defined by a replica contraction at integer replica number $n$, and the multi-entropy is its $n\to1$ limit. In holography this limit is conjectured to compute the area of a minimal soap-film web in the bulk. Understanding multi-entropy for general states, however, is harder. Unlike the bipartite case, the replica contraction is not a moment of a density matrix, and the continuation to $n=1$ has to be found by other means. We study this problem for qubit graph states. We show that at every odd $n$ the contraction equals $2^{-k/2}$, where $k$ is a sum of ranks of matrices over a finite field, one row and one column per qubit. We define a class of graphs that we call collision-controlled, for which the rank sum is a polynomial in $n$. This class includes graphs without even cycles and all complete bipartite graphs. The natural polynomial $n \to 1$ continuation is a finite sum over partitions of the parties. While the R\'enyi multi-entropy is non-increasing under single-qubit Pauli measurements at every odd integer $n>1$, the continuation to $n=1$ is not. A $Z$ measurement on one qubit of an odd ring with $2r + 1 \geq 7$ qubits raises it from $(r+1)\log 2$ to $(2r-1) \log 2$. Thus the continuation is not an entanglement monotone.
item.dc:creator: Sriram Akella, Abhijit Gadde

item.title: Broken isospectrality in inverted black hole potentials and the emergence of Efimov scaling
item.description: arXiv:2610.27102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Are the inverted Regge-Wheeler and Zerilli potentials arising in Mashhoon's bound-state approach to black-hole quasinormal modes isospectral? Extending previous numerical and analytical studies of the inverted Regge-Wheeler potential, we present the first direct computation of the bound-state spectrum of the inverted Zerilli potential. Although Chandrasekhar proved that the original potentials have identical quasinormal-mode spectra, we show that their inverted counterparts have distinct bound-state spectra. We also demonstrate that potential inversion destroys their first-order Darboux relation, used by Glampedakis et al. to provide a simpler proof of isospectrality. A continuous interpolation between the potentials reveals substantially larger energy shifts in the interior than at the endpoints, indicating cancellations that suppress the endpoint spectral splitting. Explaining this behavior requires second-order perturbative contributions, even towards the eikonal limit. Despite these differences, both spectra exhibit asymptotic geometric scaling characteristic of Efimov physics, first discovered in three-boson systems. This scaling also applies to other inverted potentials with the same leading tail, including the scalar-field case studied here. Beyond their theoretical implications, our results raise questions for recently developed methods that compute quasinormal modes with high precision from numerical bound states.
item.dc:creator: Umer Shahzad, Sebastian H. V\"olkel

item.title: Model and parameter-path dependence of charged Dirac quasi-bound spectra in Born--Infeld and Euler--Heisenberg-type geometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.27118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quasi-bound states of a charged massive Dirac field in the exact electrically charged Einstein--Born--Infeld (BI) geometry and in a leading-order Euler--Heisenberg-type (EH) approximation. The two descriptions agree in the weak-field limit. We compare families in which either the mass measured at infinity or the outer-horizon radius is held fixed, and examine several field charges and levels. We integrate the radial equations outward from the horizon and inward from large radius, then match the solutions. The resulting frequencies show that the effect of the nonlinear terms depends on both the electrodynamic theory and the chosen comparison. For the fundamental like-charge mode, the small change in its real frequency has opposite signs in the two theories when the mass is fixed, whereas it is upward in both when the horizon radius is fixed. The fundamental mode decays more slowly as the nonlinear term grows along either family. The narrowest level, however, decays more rapidly when the mass is fixed and more slowly when the horizon radius is fixed. The spectra of the two theories approach one another as the nonlinear term is reduced. We also follow several higher levels; their decay widths and their response depend on the state and on the family used for comparison. The nonlinear coefficient is used as an effective parameter and is not matched to the microscopic coupling in quantum electrodynamics (QED).
item.dc:creator: Bekir Can L\"utf\"uo\u{g}lu

item.title: Local obstructions to trapped-region escape in modified gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.27225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an ''effective'' stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. We develop a geometry-first alternative in spherical symmetry. For a normalized pair of future-directed radial null vectors, twolongitudinal Ricci projections and one independent transverse Einstein projection obey exact area-weighted transport laws. These imply a trapping-persistence theorem: after a nondegenerate future-outer marginal sphere, a regular ingoing generator cannot exit the trapped region while the ingoing longitudinal and transverse convergence channels remain nonnegative. In metric $f(R)$ gravity, with $F\equiv df/dR>0$, we then construct an entropy-resolved hierarchy based on the local Wald-density variable $Fr^2$. In the longitudinal entropy-focusing law, the scalaron second derivative cancels exactly, leaving a nonpositive scalar-gradient square together with the physical matter projection; in the independent transverse entropy-transport law, all scalaron derivative terms cancel. Entropy trapping is consequently governed by the physical matter condition $T_{nn}\geq 0$ and an algebraic mixed threshold rather than by a fictitious effective fluid. The resulting hierarchy cleanly separates matter positivity, geometric focusing, marginal-surface recovery, and gravitational-entropy evolution, and identifies the precise local reversals required for regular inner horizons, throats, and trapped-to-antitrapped transitions.
item.dc:creator: Francisco S. N. Lobo

item.title: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.27308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Contreras (UTFSM), Jose Garrido (UTFSM), Eugene Levin (Tel Aviv U.)

item.title: The $b\bar{b}c\bar{c}$ Fully Heavy Tetraquark at the LHC and the FCC: Multimodal Fragmentation and Observability
item.description: arXiv:2610.27396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the production of the all-heavy mixed-flavor $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark through a multimodal fragmentation setup combining direct-multiquark and scalar-diquark mechanisms. Standard Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution is applied while preserving threshold consistency through the Heavy-Flavor NonRelativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme. The resulting fragmentation functions (FFs) are then embedded into hybrid high-energy and collinear factorization at next-to-leading order for semi-inclusive tetraquark-plus-jet production. We compare the two mechanisms through rapidity-separation distributions at the 14 TeV High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and at the 100 TeV Future Circular Collider (FCC), finding a clear phenomenological preference for the direct-multiquark channel over the scalar-diquark mode. Integrated cross sections and expected event yields provide favorable production-level prospects for future searches at the HL-LHC, with substantially enhanced statistics at FCC energies. These results establish a quantitative connection between microscopic formation mechanisms and the prospective observability of the $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark at present and future hadron colliders.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao V. Bulh\~oes, Francesco G. Celiberto, Victor P. Gon\c{c}alves

item.title: Stability Analysis of Axion Dark Energy Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.27514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the stability of an axion dark energy model characterized by a periodic scalar-field potential motivated by pseudo Nambu Goldstone bosons. While such models are well suited to drive late-time cosmic acceleration and can exhibit rich dynamical features, including oscillatory behavior of the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, their viability crucially depends on the existence of stable cosmological solutions. By reformulating the background evolution equations as an autonomous dynamical system, we identify the fixed points corresponding to radiation-dominated, matter-dominated, and dark energy dominated epochs. Using both analytical and numerical techniques, we analyze the stability properties of these fixed points within the observationally allowed region of parameter space. Our results show that the radiation- and matter-dominated phases emerge naturally as saddle points, ensuring a standard cosmological evolution, while the late-time dark energy dominated solution acts as a stable attractor. This guarantees the robustness of cosmic acceleration against variations in initial conditions. Overall, our study establishes the axion dark energy model as a dynamically consistent and observationally viable candidate for explaining the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe.
item.dc:creator: Ankan Mukherjee, Nandan Roy

item.title: Stabilizer R\'enyi moments beyond entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2610.27596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stabilizer R\'enyi moments depend on a choice of operator basis and need not be determined by entanglement spectra. In this paper, we study their spatial decay in critical quantum chains described by two-dimensional conformal field theories. We derive an exact entanglement baseline for reductions of pure stabilizer states and a symmetry selection rule for the charged contribution at fixed support. An exact Ising example shows that an on-site rotation changes the full decay exponent while preserving every subsystem entanglement spectrum. For growing Ising intervals at index two, we obtain an exact Pfaffian representation and compare the charged amplitude with a candidate conformal boundary calculation. The data support this prediction, but its identification with the lattice limit still requires endpoint matching and control of the order of limits.
item.dc:creator: Vishnu Jejjala, Joydeep Naskar

item.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2610.27750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem from the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator through symplectic reduction. By rewriting the moment maps of the harmonic oscillator in terms of five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we identify the moment map expected to yield the Runge-Lenz vector. We then perform the reduction with respect to the SU(2) symmetry, derive the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian, and show explicitly that the identified moment map reduces to the Runge-Lenz vector.
item.dc:creator: Hitoshi Ikemori, Shinsaku Kitakado, Yoshimitsu Matsui, Toshiyuki Okubo, Toshiro Sato

item.title: Information Geometry of DGLAP Evolution: From Geodesic Tests to Emergent Small-Circle Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.27886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the geometric structure of leading-order (LO) nonsinglet DGLAP evolution on the Fisher--Rao manifold of normalized valence distributions, asking whether the QCD-selected trajectory is geodesic and how its departure from geodesic motion is organized. Through the isometric embedding $\Phi=2\sqrt{p}$, the evolution is represented as a curve on a Hilbert sphere of radius two, with its velocity and acceleration determined directly by the DGLAP operator. For a GRV98-based total-valence trajectory over $2\leq Q^2\leq 2000~{\rm GeV}^2$, we find a nonzero but weakly scale-dependent geodesic curvature. An arc-length-weighted principal-component analysis shows that two affine directions capture more than $99.999\%$ of the trajectory variance. The corresponding affine plane intersects the Fisher sphere in a small circle, whose predicted geodesic curvature closely agrees with that reconstructed from the DGLAP-generated acceleration. An $x$-resolved analysis further reveals that Fisher motion is governed by relative PDF reshaping rather than probability weight alone, with different momentum-fraction regions contributing to motion along the trajectory and its transverse bending. The Mellin representation provides a complementary perspective on the effective dimensional reduction through the collective evolution of the spectral hierarchy. These results establish a quantitative information-geometric characterization of the reference LO DGLAP trajectory and reveal an organized, near-small-circle structure over the finite evolution interval.
item.dc:creator: Wei Kou, Xurong Chen

item.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.27903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Dmitrii Pavlov, Rainer Sinn

item.title: Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli
item.description: arXiv:2610.27934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Kydonakis, Lutian Zhao

item.title: Field theories and critical excitations at anyon condensation transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anyon condensation transitions remain challenging to characterize especially when the condensing anyons are non-abelian. We develop two complementary approaches for extracting information about the transition from the categorical data of the parent topological order and the condensate. The first adapts a Ginzburg-Landau procedure developed for $1+1$D transitions in the SymTFT setting to $2+1$D anyon condensation transitions. The construction applies when the anyons participating in the condensate have integer quantum dimensions. The second gives a criterion for identifying which point and loop excitations become critical at a continuous transition. The key step is to determine which anyon loops remain condensed throughout. All other loops become critical, while a point excitation becomes critical if it braids trivially with every condensed loop. We illustrate both proposals in several abelian and non-abelian examples.
item.dc:creator: Luisa Eck, Xie Chen

item.title: Black Holes are about Quantum Information
item.description: arXiv:2610.28185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review and analyse quantum information-theoretic approaches to black hole evaporation that purport to bring us closer to a resolution of the black hole information paradox. Our focus is on the Page-time paradox and on the contribution of the Hayden-Preskill model to understanding information release under the assumption of unitary evaporation. In this model, the black hole is taken to be a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics can be represented by a quantum circuit, and its information-processing and communication abilities are studied. We identify the assumptions underlying this modelling and highlight two key features, fast scrambling dynamics and entanglement as a resource, that underpin the information release in the model. We argue that this reasoning exemplifies a broader change in how information is used in black hole physics, in which quantum information theory now provides a useful operational modelling framework. This application avoids earlier philosophical objections insofar as it is not based on epistemic ignorance and does not regard information as a substance. This line of reasoning has become central to the debate and, as such, warrants greater attention from the philosophy of physics community.
item.dc:creator: Aude Corbeel, Sebastian De Haro

item.title: Soft Breaking Naturalness in Majorana Fermion Loop induced Scalar and Majoron Amplitudes
item.description: arXiv:2610.28198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Majorana fermion loops contribute a shift-symmetry violating effective potential to the coupled scalar field. When the Majorana fermion is light, a larger number of symmetry violating insertions let the loop contribution to grow increasingly infrared sensitive to the Majorana mass. With explicit calculations, we calculate the symmetry violating amplitudes, show that the scalar potential's natural scales serve as nonzero kinematic matching points which remove the superficial sensitivity to the symmetry-violating Majorana mass, continuously restoring the shift symmetry in agreement with 't Hooft naturalness. In the spontaneous broken phase, the scalar radial vacuum expectation value readily ensures the infrared safety of symmetry violating Majorana fermion loops, and all $n$-point Majoron functions develop a leading linear dependence on the symmetry violating parameter in the soft breaking limit, which matches the expansion of the Coleman-Weinberg determinant.
item.dc:creator: Mussawir Khan, Wei Chao, Yu Gao

item.title: Proliferation Transitions for Quantum Doubles of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Proliferation transitions are phase transitions between a 2+1d topological order $\mathcal{T}$ and another $\mathcal{T}/\mathcal{A}$, obtained by condensing anyons in an algebra $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathcal{T}$. We consider such transitions in quantum doubles of groups, $\mathcal{T}=D(G, \omega)$, for finite groups $G$ possibly with three-cocycle $\omega$, for which condensable algebras are fully classified. Given a condensable algebra $\mathcal{A}$, we represent $\mathcal{T}$ in terms of a Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), that is tailored to the $\mathcal{A}$ proliferation transition. The SymTFT bulk is constructed from the M\"uger center of the subcategory generated by the algebra, i.e. the category of transparent lines, which can be bosons or fermions. Properties of the transition can then be inferred directly from the algebra classification data. For gauged Landau-Ginzburg (LG*) type transitions, we show that they do not only depend on the anyons in $\mathcal{A}$ through their field content, but the cubic interactions are fixed in terms of the multiplication structure of $\mathcal{A}$. Applied to twin algebras, which have the same anyon content but different multiplication structures, we show that twins result in distinct proliferation transitions.
item.dc:creator: Yuhan Gai, Sakura Schafer-Nameki

item.title: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
item.description: arXiv:2610.28283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Precision electroweak predictions for future $e^+e^-$ colliders will require levels of precision unmatched in collider physics and the modelling of multiple-photon emissions, and the exponentiation of the associated logarithms needs to be carefully considered. The Yennie-Frautschi-Suura theorem subtracts the infrared singularities to all orders and exponentiates them, leaving infrared-finite remainders which can be calculated order-by-order. Coherent exponentiation performs this subtraction at the amplitude level, preserving the interference between emissions, but has so far been available only for fermion-pair production, with hand-coded amplitudes. We present ACRAIC, an automated, amplitude-level realization of this subtraction for general scattering processes in Sherpa. This method allows us to construct an $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ amplitude level subtraction scheme, in which the infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by the Berends--Giele recursion, and the one-loop electroweak virtual enters through a per-helicity factor from the loop provider. At $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ two independent matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to $\sim10^{-3}$, and the estimated perturbative uncertainty shrinks by about an order of magnitude relative to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$.
item.dc:creator: Alan Price

item.title: Topological ModMax--AdS Black Holes: Extremality, Charge Normalization, and Limits of WGC Diagnostics
item.description: arXiv:2610.28359v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study four-dimensional topological anti-de Sitter black holes sourced by ModMax electrodynamics and its sign-reversed counterpart. Distinguishing the field-strength amplitude from the conserved displacement flux fixes the charge normalization, potential, and first law. We classify the exact extremal roots for spherical, planar, and hyperbolic horizons; in particular, the hyperbolic ModMax branch has no upper-charge discriminant bound and contains a finite-charge zero-mass point. We also derive the unstable spherical null circular orbit and evaluate the local near-horizon AdS$_2$ Breitenlohner--Freedman index for an explicitly specified charged-scalar probe. These are classical diagnostics, not a WGC verdict: the model does not specify a charged-particle spectrum, an ultraviolet completion, or the global perturbation problem. The distance and de Sitter conjectures cannot be quantitatively tested with the fixed-coupling AdS data considered here.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Noori Gashti, Behnam Pourhassan, Saheb Soroushfar

item.title: Geometrically Induced Semiclassical Limit for Quasinormal Modes and Greybody Factors in Higher-Dimensional Near-Ultracold spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.28367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and greybody factors (GBFs) in higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordst\"{o}m--de Sitter black holes based on the massless scalar field. Our analysis focuses on the QNMs in the near-ultracold family where the inner, outer, and cosmological horizons are close together. Under the geometric limit condition, the leading-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin term of the QNM is dominant for fixed angular quantum numbers and dimensionality without imposing the eikonal limit. Particularly, the corresponding GBFs also retain the explicit form of both parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the half-transmission frequency of the GBF and its derivative are related to null geodesics, in terms of aspects such as the angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent, with the use of both parameters. We provide their relationships in arbitrary dimensionality. Furthermore, the higher-order corrections to the QNMs are investigated at the Nariai limit and in the near-ultracold geometry with separated horizons.
item.dc:creator: Bogeun Gwak

item.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
item.description: arXiv:2610.28526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and dlog-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlator, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a user-friendly Mathematica package MadStree for computing arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlators.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Chen, Yi-Xiao Tao, Xinyi Wang, Dong Zhang

item.title: Slow-Roll Inflation at Arbitrary Order
item.description: arXiv:2610.28608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive explicit expressions for the primordial scalar and tensor spectra at arbitrary finite order $p$ in the slow-roll expansion, valid both for canonical single-field inflation and $k$-inflation. At any order, the spectra are determined by known combinations of slow-roll parameters weighted by universal coefficients entirely fixed by the free de Sitter solutions, without requiring perturbatively corrected mode functions. Using these spectra, we obtain closed-form consistency relations that connect the tensor tilt $n_t$ and its runnings $\alpha_n^t\equiv d^n n_t/d(\ln k)^n$ to the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, the scalar spectral index $n_s$, and its runnings $\alpha_n^s\equiv d^n(n_s-1)/d(\ln k)^n$. The consistency relations are valid for arbitrary $n\geq 0$ and any finite $p\geq 0$, without recursion over lower-order relations. For $k$-inflation, they additionally depend on the scalar sound speed and its scale derivatives. We develop an algorithm that generates both the spectra and consistency relations for any pair $(n,p)$. We reproduce known results through next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) and extend the explicit calculations up to N10LO.
item.dc:creator: William Giar\`e

item.title: Inflationary Particle Production and the Swampland
item.description: arXiv:2512.07930v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the impact of particle production during inflation in scenarios where an infinite tower of states features a mass scale that decreases exponentially along the inflationary trajectory. Such couplings naturally arise in string effective field theories and are in fact motivated by the Swampland Distance Conjecture (SDC). We show that the corrections to inflationary observables sourced by the tower scale as $(H/\Lambda_{\text{sp}})^{2+p}$, with $H$ being the Hubble scale, $\Lambda_{\text{sp}}$ being the species scale, that is the quantum gravity cut-off, and $p\geq 1$ characterizes the density of states in the tower. As a result, in gravitationally weakly coupled cosmological effective theories, the tower-induced contributions are suppressed relative to the standard single-field predictions, leaving the inflationary phenomenology essentially unchanged. We demonstrate this explicitly across a set of well-motivated inflationary potentials, and we compare the resulting predictions with the most recent observational constraints, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope.
item.dc:creator: Dieter L\"ust, Joaquin Masias, Mauro Pieroni, Marco Scalisi

item.title: The JLMS formula in a large code with approximate error correction
item.description: arXiv:2601.00442v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gauge/gravity duality is often described as a quantum error correcting code. However, as seen in the Jafferis-Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Suh (JLMS) formula, exact quantum error correction with complementary recovery (and thus entanglement wedge reconstruction) emerges only in the limit $G \to 0$. As a result, precise arguments controlling error terms have focused on what we call `small' codes which, as $G \to 0$, describe only perturbative excitations near a given classical solution. Such settings are quite restrictive and, in particular, they prohibit discussion of any modular flow that would change the classical background. As a result, they forbid consideration of modular flows generated by semiclassical bulk states at order-one modular parameters. In contrast, we present a single `large' code for the bulk theory that can accommodate such flows and, in particular, in the $G \to 0$ limit includes superpositions of states associated with distinct classical backgrounds. This large code is assembled from small codes that each satisfy an approximate Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena formula. In this extended setting we clarify the meaning of the (approximate) JLMS relation between bulk and boundary modular Hamiltonians and quantify its validity in an appropriate class of states.
item.dc:creator: Xi Dong, Donald Marolf, Pratik Rath

item.title: Heavy holographic correlators in defect conformal field theories
item.description: arXiv:2601.15736v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study holographic defect conformal field theories which are dual to probe branes with bottom-up methods. First we determine the embedding of codimension-1 interface branes in AdS space. Then we compute defect one and two-point functions of heavy scalar operators at strong coupling. We use geodesic approximations to compute reflected two-point functions in two ways, as well as ambient and defect-channel two-point functions. In appropriate limits, our results agree with the operator product expansion (OPE) and the boundary operator expansion (BOE).
item.dc:creator: Georgios Linardopoulos, Chanyong Park

item.title: Magic and Wormholes in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
item.description: arXiv:2602.12339v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Any quantum state is fully specified by the expectation values of a complete set of Hermitian operators. For a system of Majorana fermions, such as the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, this set of observables can be taken to be all possible strings of Majorana fermion operators. The expectation values of these fermion strings in a thermal state depend erratically on the microscopic couplings that specify the SYK Hamiltonian, and we study their statistical properties directly in the thermodynamic limit using path integral techniques. When the underlying SYK Hamiltonian is chaotic, we find that these expectation values are well-modeled as real Gaussian random variables with zero mean and a variance that we compute.
